answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock tokens in a public stake contract before it votes or earns rewards. Voting weight is proportional to locked value, so dividing one stake among many identities adds no influence; provable fraud triggers slashing. A lantern dashboard can show stakes, timber can secure the audit log, and a mirror check can flag coordinated accounts. The attacker must tie up capital and risk losing it, rather than create costless names.
